name: Slayer Bloody Jake — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Slayer Bloody Jake from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's page "Bloody Jake" but are not part of the Slayer Bloody Jake entry, which is unchanged.

Bloody jakes are cruel backwoods folk who use their skills and familiarity with the home turf to prey upon their kin and neighbors along with any travelers who mistakenly enter their domain.

Requirements
Alignment: A bloody jake must be evil. A bloody jake that becomes non-evil cannot gain new levels in this class but retain all their class abilities.
Class Features
Favored Terrain (Ex)

Arcane Preparations (Sp) You put bits and bobs into your traps that lower the defenses of your prey. On a failed save, in addition to the trap’s normal function, the target takes a penalty to saves against your spells and Cruel tricks equal to the number of arcane preparations advanced tactics you possess. Additionally the target takes double the same penalty on their spell resistance, if any.
Assassination (Ex) You traps are more devious and deadly. You add your assassination combat die to any damage dealt by your trap on a failed save.
Battlefield Domination (Ex) You know tricks to make your traps more concussive and explosive. When a creature fails their save against the trap, they take extra damage equal to your battlefield domination advanced tactic die. Additionally, the creature(s) are shunted back 5 feet directly away from the trap. This increases to 10 feet if they fail their save against the trap by 10 or more.
Capturing (Ex) When crafting your trap you include poisons, powders, and bludgeons to render your foe unconscious. When a creature is subject to your trap they take an additional amount of nonlethal damage equal to your capturing advanced tactic damage die. If the triggering creature is immune to nonlethal damage, they instead take 1 damage per capturing advanced tactic damage die.
Creature Hunting (Ex) You can tailor your traps to best harm particular types of prey. When placing the trap you designate a creature type similar to a ranger’s favored enemy. If a creature of the chosen type is affected by the trap, they take additional damage equal to your creature hunting advanced tactic bonus die.
Defensive Posture (Ex) You know how to make your prey more vulnerable with your traps. When the target fails their save against the trap, they take a penalty to AC equal to your defensive posture advanced tactic bonus damage dice, to a minimum of their touch AC. This penalty lasts for 1d6 rounds.
Dueling Stance (Ex) When making the trap, you make it very effective against single foes. If the trap targets a single foe, increase the DC by the dueling stance advanced tactic bonus you have. Additionally the target of the trap is inflicted with bleed equal to the dueling stance advanced tactic for 1d4 rounds.
Frantic Fighting (Ex) When making the trap you add in a bunch of extra rocks, shrapnel, and whatever else you can find to make it explode. You deal your frantic fighting advanced tactic damage to all creatures within 5 feet of the trap when it is triggered. This does not deal extra damage to the creature that triggered the trap, unless they are a size larger than you.
Magical Disruption (Su) When making this trap you put in bits and bobs known to disrupt tricky magics of your prey, like bits of star metal, bells, etc. If the target triggering the trap casts spells, they take the extra damage and concentration penalty imposed by your magical disruption advanced tactic.
Maneuverability (Ex) When placing the trap, you add in small bits that cause pain in the target’s limbs. It reduces their movement speed(s) by half for 1 hour per maneuverability advanced tactic damage die. This penalty to movement can be ended early if they receive magical healing or treat deadly wounds.
Mounted Maneuvers (Ex) When placing the trap you add in some extra snares. If the target fails the save against the trap, the trap pins them in place for 1 round per mounted maneuvers advanced tactic damage die you possess. While trapped in this way, their movement speeds are reduced to 0, but they otherwise retain their Dexterity and defenses.
Natural Connection (Sp) When crafting the trap you add in animal calls or other bits that animals in the area would be attracted to. When the trap is triggered it casts a summon nature’s ally spell of the highest level you can cast. This special casting of summon nature’s ally lasts for 1 minute per caster level instead of 1 round or until the target of the trap is killed or incapacitated.
Non-Conventional Weaponry (Ex) When crafting the trap you can add the effect of an alchemical item (or bomb) to it. When the trap springs it applies the effect of the alchemical item using the trap’s save DC in place of the item’s normal save DC.
Psychic Attenuation (Sp) When crafting this trap, you add in items of psychic significance to you and instill it with a psychic spell. You can use one of your spells per day to have it trigger when the trap is triggered. The target of the spell is the target of the trap or the area of the spell is centered on the trap.
Protective Prayers (Sp) When crafting the trap, you add in small prayers and other religious markings instilling it with a spell. You can use one of your spells per day to have it trigger when the trap is triggered. The target of the spell is the target of the trap or the area of the spell is centered on the trap.
Sniping (Ex) When placing the trap you add in some extra snares. If the target fails the save against the trap, the trap pins them in place for 1 round per sniping advanced tactic damage die you possess. While trapped in this way, their movement speeds are reduced to 0, but they otherwise retain their Dexterity and defenses.
Spirit Slaying (Su) When making this trap you tie in fetishes and other spiritual accoutrement. The trap can trigger on spirit creatures, even if they normally would not, and if it does, it deals your extra spirit slaying damage to the spirit creature. If the trap triggers on a possessed creature. The possessed creature suffers the effects of the trap, while the possessing spirit takes the spirit slaying damage.
Team Maneuvers (Ex) You tie in a painful burr into the trap that on a failed save gets stuck into the target. Your kin know how to take advantage of it to cause extra pain. The next time an ally attacks the target of the trap, they deal your extra flanking damage. This extra damage only triggered once per trap.
Volley Fire (Ex) You tie in a bundle of arrows or other sharp bits into the trap. The trap always deals the minimum damage you would deal if you missed with the volley advanced tactic, even if they make the save against the trap. The traps can have multiple advanced tactic bonuses, but the conditions for each are triggered separately.
Can’t Run-Can’t Hide (Sp)

At 14th level, a bloody jake can move with supernatural ease while in their favored terrain. Once per day, they may travel as if using the dimension door spell with a caster level equal to their class level. They cannot take any allies with them when teleporting in this manner. After the first use of this ability, the bloody jake may use a use of their Cruel tricks to use this ability again.
